memories.content: The user's project's CI is failing on the Node 18 job.
The user's project uses `crypto.hash()`, which was added in Node 20.12 and 21.7, causing tests to fail on Node 18.
The user does not want to use polyfills or `createHash` fallback branches for compatibility shims, as they consider them to rot.
The user's project's CI test matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs tests on Node 20 and 22.
The `engines.node` entry in the user's project's `package.json` is set to `>=20`.
The user's project's README under Requirements states that Node 20 or newer is required because it uses `crypto.hash`, which was added in 20.12.
The user's project's CI jobs for Node 20 and 22 are passing.
The user's project standardized on pnpm in January 2026.
The install section of the user's project's README now uses `pnpm install`, and the scripts section references `pnpm test` and `pnpm build`.
The Quick start section of the user's project's README still includes an npm-based one-liner that uses `npx` to run the published CLI.
The user's orders report is timing out.
The user's `orders` table has approximately 40 million rows in production.
In December 2025, the user experienced a production issue where a plain `CREATE INDEX` command locked writes for several minutes on the `orders` table.

The user's project migration runner (db/run-migrations.ts) wraps every migration in `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` by default. To run a migration with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, which cannot execute inside a transaction block, the migration module must export `disableTransaction = true`.
The user's project uses a migration naming convention of `<timestamp>_<snake_description>.ts` for files in `db/migrations`.

The user's migration `db/migrations/20260304_add_orders_customer_created_idx.ts` includes a comment explaining that `disableTransaction = true` is necessary because `CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction, and the runner wraps migrations in one unless this flag is set.
The user is on-call rotation this week.
The user's `TestAggregate` in `internal/metrics` fails about one in five runs on CI, but passes locally every time.

The user's `TestAggregate` in `internal/metrics` was failing due to non-deterministic map iteration order in Go. The fix involved modifying the `Aggregate()` function in `aggregate.go` to collect keys, sort them with `slices.Sort`, and then build the result in that sorted order. This resolved the flakiness, with 200 out of 200 test runs now passing.
The user wants the race detector to be enabled on every CI run, even if it increases the job duration.

The user added `-race` to the `test` target in the Makefile to enable the race detector on CI runs. This increased the CI run time from 1 minute 10 seconds to 2 minutes 40 seconds, and no races were reported.

The user's portfolio site generates 1x and 2x image variants using `sharp` in a build step (`scripts/resize-images.ts`).

The user's weather ETL job, `etl/weather_daily.py`, fails with a MemoryError when processing a 12 GB parquet dump.
The user decided to rewrite the `etl/weather_daily.py` script using Polars.
The user wants the output of the rewritten ETL job to be identical to the original, specifically the `daily_weather.parquet` file, because downstream dashboards depend on it.

When using Polars for ETL, to avoid `MemoryError` when writing to parquet, the user needs to combine `collect(engine='streaming')` with `sink_parquet` because the streaming engine is opt-in per query in Polars 1.x.

When migrating the `etl/weather_daily.py` script from pandas to Polars, the user had to cast Polars' Date type to Datetime to match pandas' datetime64[ns] type, ensuring compatibility with downstream readers.
The new `daily_weather.parquet` file generated by the Polars script has 3,652 rows and the same column set as the pandas version.
The user started the full weather ETL job and went for lunch. The job was estimated to take about 9 minutes in total.

The user's MusicPlayer project, written in Kotlin and using media3, experienced playback stopping when the screen locked on a Pixel 8 (Android 14). Playback worked fine on an older Samsung device running Android 12.

To fix playback stopping when the screen locks on Android 14 devices for the MusicPlayer project, the user added `android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback"` to the `PlaybackService` entry in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` and declared the `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK` permission. This resolved a `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` that occurred about 10 seconds after the screen locked.

The user committed the change to declare the `mediaPlayback` foreground service type for Android 14 with the message "Declare the mediaPlayback foreground service type for Android 14". The target SDK is 34, so this change applies to users on Android 14 or newer.
The user prefers commit messages to be in the imperative mood, without emojis, and without a 'fix:' prefix, as they do not use conventional commits.
The user decided to drop the Samsung device from their test devices because it runs Android 12, and they believe no one uses the app below Android 13.
The user set `minSdk = 33` in `app/build.gradle.kts` for the MusicPlayer project and removed two `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 31` guards that became redundant.
The user is rewriting the token-saver CLI in Rust.
The primary target for the token-saver CLI is Windows, with Linux and macOS to follow.
The user prefers to use `clap`'s derive API for argument parsing in the token-saver CLI, valuing the typed struct over saving a dependency.

Spawning `powershell -Command` on the user's machine takes about 1.9 seconds due to the user profile loading (which imports oh-my-posh and two modules). Using `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` reduces the spawn time to about 180 ms.

The user adopted the fix of using `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` for the proxy subcommand in the token-saver CLI to improve performance, reducing `rtk proxy git status` from 2.1s to 0.3s.
A comment was added to the token-saver CLI code above the spawn explaining the 1.9s profile load and why `-NoProfile` is used.

The user's project now includes a startup check in settings.py that fails fast with a clear message if any required secrets are empty, preventing containers from starting if secrets are missing.

The user's deploy checklist in docs/deploy.md now includes `python manage.py check --deploy` and a `scripts/verify-env.sh` step. The script compares variable names in .env.example against the target host's environment and exits non-zero if any names are missing.
The `scripts/verify-env.sh` script ran against production and found no missing environment variables.

The user had an incident on 2026-04-02 where a renamed environment variable (`STRIPE_WH_SECRET` to `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) was not present in production, causing Stripe webhook failures. The incident was resolved by manually setting the variable.
The user's staging environment for the project had its .env regenerated with the new `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` name on 2026-03-28.

The user had an incident report written in docs/incidents/2026-04-02-stripe-webhooks.md, detailing the timeline (14:10 deploy, 14:12 first 400, 14:35 fixed), the cause (renamed env var not present in prod), and the two implemented guards, with a link to docs/deploy.md.
